properties.name: A budget is what makes optimisation stop
properties.rationale:
THE FIRST PERFORMANCE BUDGET THIS PROJECT HAS EVER STATED, and it was written BEFORE the code was touched, on purpose. `con:graph-construction-is-setup-not-work` (1 ms) was derived rather than picked: construction is setup, so a caller that builds a graph and does twenty writes should spend most of its time on the writes.

THE CAUSE, found by measuring rather than guessing: `open_in_memory` cost 41.3 ms against 54.7 us for an `add_capability` write - 750x - because `load_schema()` re-parsed and re-merged eleven include_str!'d YAML documents on every call, in a binary where those bytes are fixed at compile time.

THE FIX caches the parsed Result in a LazyLock. The Result and not the Schema, so a malformed domain still fails loud on every call; and `load_schema()` hands out a CLONE, because StorageEngine takes the schema by value and two graphs must not share one.

WHAT THE BUDGET BOUGHT: the first re-measurement read 2.79 ms - a 14.8x speedup AND OVER BUDGET. Without a number written down beforehand that is exactly where the work stops. The warm figure was 266 us, under budget, so it stopped there - leaving the obvious next move (Arc instead of cloning, worth 252 of those 266 us) undone because it needs a dependency's API in another repo. A defensible stopping point at a repo boundary.

TWO LESSONS FOUND BY DOING. (1) A DURATION ASSERTION IN A PARALLEL SUITE MEASURES CONTENTION: the first durable test asserted 5 ms, measured 266 us alone and 6 ms inside `cargo test --workspace`, and failed. The usual response - raise the threshold until it stops complaining - retires the gate without anyone deciding to. It now asserts a cold-versus-warm RATIO, which survives contention because both halves are slowed equally and which pins the thing that actually broke. AN OPTIMISATION GUARD SHOULD ASSERT THE STRUCTURE THAT MAKES CODE FAST, NOT THE TIME IT TAKES. (2) OPTIMISATION IS WHERE ARCHITECTURAL RULES GET TRADED AWAY: the LazyLock tripped `no_per_design_process_globals`, whose own words are 'the door closes one convenient static at a time, each individually reasonable'. Paying it cost one paragraph stating why a compile-time-embedded schema is a fact about the BINARY and not about any design.
properties.summary: The schema is parsed once per process instead of once per graph: construction 41.3ms -> 266us, suite 191.8s -> 96.5s.
